title: Beyond the 956: San Antonio Fires Officer Marcus Bazan, Indicted on 2019 Sexual Assault Counts — Five Years Before He Was Hired
excerpt: San Antonio police fired Officer Marcus Bazan, 30, after a Bexar County grand jury indicted him on two counts of sexual assault tied to alleged acts from June 2019 — five years before the department hired him.
content:
The San Antonio Police Department has fired Officer Marcus Bazan, 30, after a Bexar County grand jury indicted him on November 18, 2026, on two counts of sexual assault tied to alleged acts from June 2019 — five years before the department hired him.

Court records show the alleged offense date was June 22, 2019, and both counts are second-degree felonies. Bazan was booked into the Bexar County Jail on November 18 and placed on administrative duty.

He was not an SAPD officer when the alleged acts happened. A Texas Commission on Law Enforcement record lists his appointment as an SAPD peace officer beginning August 2, 2024.

The timeline is the story. SAPD received a report in 2024 alleging Bazan committed sexual assault in 2019. The department investigated the allegation in 2024 — after he was already on the force — and referred the case to the Bexar County District Attorney's Office. KSAT first reported the investigation came before his hiring, then corrected itself: the investigation came after he was hired.

Police Chief Jesse Salame fired Bazan following the indictment.

Bazan is the 11th SAPD officer arrested in 2026, according to KSAT Investigates.

Bazan has not entered a plea, and details about the victim have not been made public. He is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Update — November 24, 2026

Bazan was released after posting a $65,000 bond the same day he was booked, Nov. 18, according to El Tejano RGV and a Bexar County booking record (case 2026CR013980). The case is in the 186th District Court, where Judge Kristina Escalona is presiding. Bond conditions include no contact with the victim, a weekly check-in call with the court, and no possessing, using or buying a gun. No arraignment or plea has been reported yet. The charges are allegations, and Bazan is presumed innocent until proven guilty in court.

Sources: KSAT 12 (Samuel Rocha IV, Sean Talbot, Nov. 18, 2026); San Antonio Express-News (Annasofia Scheve); San Antonio Current (Nov. 19, 2026); San Antonio Police Department statement; Bexar County court records; El Tejano RGV (Nov. 20, 2026); Bexar County booking record.
